title: Database Ossuary
description: Relational schemas, primary keys, indexing, and ACID transactions.

questions.prompt: What key property distinguishes a Primary Key in relational databases?
options: It can contain multiple NULL values
It must uniquely identify every record and cannot be NULL
It can only store positive integers
questions.evidence_quote: A primary key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain NULL values.
questions.explanation: Primary keys enforce entity integrity across database rows.

questions.prompt: Which normal form requires removing transitive dependencies between non-key attributes?
questions.evidence_quote: Third Normal Form (3NF) requires the table to be in 2NF and have no transitive functional dependencies.
questions.explanation: 3NF ensures all non-key columns depend directly on the primary key, and nothing else.

questions.prompt: What constraint ensures that a foreign key matches an existing primary key in another table?
questions.evidence_quote: Referential integrity guarantees that foreign key relationships between tables remain consistent and valid.
questions.explanation: Referential integrity prevents orphan records in relational databases.

questions.prompt: In the ACID acronym, what does Atomicity guarantee?
options: All operations in a transaction succeed together or all are rolled back
Data is immediately cached in RAM
Transactions execute on a single CPU core
Backups are saved atom by atom
questions.evidence_quote: Atomicity ensures that all statements within a transaction are executed as a single indivisible unit: either all succeed or none take effect.
questions.explanation: Atomicity is the all-or-nothing property of database transactions.

questions.prompt: Which tree data structure is most commonly used for relational database table indexing?
questions.evidence_quote: Most relational database management systems use B+ Trees for indices to keep data sorted and allow searches, sequential access, and insertions in logarithmic time.
questions.explanation: B+ Trees minimize disk I/O operations through high fan-out nodes.

questions.prompt: What concurrency anomaly occurs when one transaction reads uncommitted changes written by another concurrent transaction?
questions.evidence_quote: A dirty read occurs when a transaction is permitted to read data from a row that has been modified by another running transaction and not yet committed.
questions.explanation: Dirty reads happen in the Read Uncommitted isolation level.

questions.prompt: Which deadlock resolution technique cancels one of the conflicting transactions and rolls back its changes?
questions.evidence_quote: When a deadlock cycle is detected by the lock manager, the database selects one transaction as a victim and rolls it back to break the cycle.
questions.explanation: Victim selection terminates one cycle node so other transactions can proceed.
